description: Log a cleaning or maintenance job against a piece of equipment. A task that takes the thing apart opens a calibration epoch, and every recipe locked before it is read through that epoch's offset — so record the offset here if you counted the clicks while reassembling, which is the one moment anybody actually knows it. Any task in the maintenance vocabulary can be logged against a grinder or machine it belongs to — including one the maker advises against, because the log records what was done. Read each piece of equipment's tasks, their intervals and their due state from list_grinders and list_machines.

details.description: Fields specific to this task. Which ones a task takes is published as details_fields on each task; a burr clean takes none

disturbs_zero.description: Whether this job disturbed the reference the stored numbers are read against — for a burr clean, whether the burrs actually came out. Defaults to the task's own answer; send 0 for a wipe-down that left the collar alone

equipment_id.description: The ID of that piece of equipment

equipment_kind.description: Which kind of equipment this job was done on

evidence.description: One line recording what the measurement rested on, e.g. "Counted 6 clicks coarser at reassembly."

guide_id.description: Optional — the id of the maintenance guide that was followed. Must be a guide for this task

note.description: Optional — what you did, and anything that surprised you

offset_source.description: How the offset was arrived at: pull (a reference shot), counted (clicks counted at reassembly), typed (asserted directly)

offset_value.description: The correction, if you measured it now: clicks to ADD to a pre-clean reading to get the same grind today, signed along the collar's own number direction. Omit it and the epoch stays unmeasured, which is a state the app shows rather than a zero it assumes

performed_at.description: When it was done (ISO 8601 or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS, UTC). Defaults to now; backdating is fine

name: log_maintenance
title: Log maintenance
